body:
## Owner request — 2026-10-12

> With the red light issue, one thing we should do is look at ROCKNIX upstream and see if this is something that might have been fixed there. There is a chance that maybe we're running with our build having an outdated issue that's been fixed upstream already. In general, if they do have a new full release, we'll want to think about our rebasing strategy.

## Verified starting point

D-WORKFLOW-111 freezes0.0.1 at9fd38fa87094d4f0e956d03ac6c660fe4fd5e9d6 (September29). Latest full ROCKNIX release is20261001, c445081a59518f37d9776e5412dd7b14910696f7,11commits beyond that base. Upstream next observed October12 isd59bdaa28908f7266e40172e088ec40813fd3f46,205commits beyond base/194beyond release. Fetching history did not merge, rebase or alter product pins.

#534 comparison: H700 LED implementation/dispatcher/flash helper are byte-identical in our firmware, frozen base, latest release and current next. Upstream batteryplus/H700LEDquirks/RGSPdts have no change across the latter range. New RK3326 EE-clone battery LED fixes target different hardware. Current RG SP red is a preserved fixed preference, with no applicable missing upstream LED fix established.

There are meaningful integration deltas: ABL1.1.9→1.2 (release notes show logo/SoC notices, no claimed fix for #558); FEX packaging, DuckStation execution, later common settings/flock changes, memory/ZRAM/oomd, suspend and kernel changes. Review exact component applicability and preserve fork behavior.

## Settled policy and remaining procedure

The cadence is already settled by D-WORKFLOW-116: take in new ROCKNIX monthly builds between fork release cycles, allow intermediary fork releases, and do not merge upstream during qualification. D-WORKFLOW-111 freezes the first release at the September29 base until0.0.1 is published; its documented exception is an applicable upstream security fix, with a register row naming the exact commit and candidate. D-WORKFLOW-117 chooses tracking with a budgeted exit: measure upstream-owned diff size, patch-refresh effort and ES conflict cost; review imported scripts/workflows before execution; reopen pin-versus-track if two cadences exceed the predeclared budget, two are skipped, or pinning is chosen. Those decisions are not reopened by this issue.

What remains to define is the operational procedure and commit-level intake. Recommended implementation: a reviewed merge from a pinned release tag on an isolated integration branch, preserving published next history; reserve rebase for unpublished topic work. Use explicit cherry-picks/backports for selected fixes between integrations, with dependency closure, upstream provenance, duplicate detection and regression evidence. During the current freeze, a non-security upstream backport would need an explicit recorded refinement of D-WORKFLOW-111. No such refinement or selected commit list exists here. Keep accepted candidate bytes immutable; qualify changes with package/build checks, clean and retained VM suites, cloud preservation and targeted device evidence. The broad monthly tracking policy stands; this is not a decision to follow only selected commits indefinitely.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Record verified upstream release/next identities, delta and applicable device/security fixes with source links. Initial snapshot: docs/qa-logs/2026-10-12-upstream-review/.
- [ ] Compare the fork overlay and likely conflicts, including settings/cloud/bootloader/ES/kernel, and document an integration plan and rollback/reference strategy.
- [ ] Resolve timing against D-WORKFLOW-111 explicitly before changing the release base; do not infer a broad rebase from a bug investigation.
- [ ] Operationalize the existing D-WORKFLOW-116/117 cadence with a predeclared integration-cost budget, release/next separation, required clean/retained/device evidence and an adopted/deferred/backport disposition per upstream intake. Do not ask the owner to choose the cadence again.

Future process work, not a new firmware run or current publication approval. #534 owns LED diagnosis; #558 owns Nova shutdown/bootloader incident.


Initial source comparison is published in afb6cb4ef7: https://github.com/pixelelated/distribution/tree/afb6cb4ef7287b30ca91ec015a8ee7d304c66844/docs/qa-logs/2026-10-12-upstream-review . Both hosted checks passed. Future implementation/review criteria remain open.


## October12 reconciliation and precise stable-release delta

> Did we ever make a determination on what we may have found in the latest stable release from ROCKNIX and what we want our rebase and likely selective rebase strategy to be with that?

The earlier issue/README wording treated too much as a proposal: D-WORKFLOW-116/117 had already settled the cadence and track-versus-pin policy on October1. Only implementation mechanics, the predeclared cost budget and selective commit intake remain open. This correction changes no decision or source pin.

Latest full release rechecked via GitHub releases/latest:20261001 atc445081a59518f37d9776e5412dd7b14910696f7. Its delta from the frozen base is11commits including merge commits,12files. This differs from the much larger post-release next delta:

- `f2148e8061` DuckStation executable permission: our accepted bc9dfe8141 recipe already uses `install -m 0755`, so this particular fix is present by equivalent implementation. No cherry-pick needed for that behavior.
- `e348c457e5` FEX Nix package-set pin: build-reproducibility/compatibility item to assess against our accepted FEX artifacts and build environment; not selected for backport.
- `51bebf5e1d` Steam runtime refresh and library-link handling: relevant to that optional installation flow; evaluate failure/preservation behavior before intake, not a proven Nova shutdown fix.
- `b354bfe6d6` ABL1.2: potential future update; release notes do not establish a fix for #558 and #528 source coverage remains unresolved.
- `7b4da83200` / `2d47bf198e` SM8250 Mangmi DP/audio work: other boards, not RG SP/H700 or Nova/SM8550.

No new applicable H700 LED fix was found. Broader settings/flock, memory/ZRAM/oomd, suspend and kernel changes discussed in the initial research belong to later upstream next, not this11-commit stable-release delta. None is selected here. No merge/rebase/cherry-pick, trial integration or new build has been run.


## Superseding base selection — #563

The owner now selects ROCKNIX20261001 as the next0.0.1 foundation. D-WORKFLOW-161 supersedes the September29 base portion of D-WORKFLOW-111 for this new qualification cycle. #563 owns this concrete integration and fresh proof; this issue retains the reusable procedure/cost-budget work. Earlier no-intake language above is the pre-selection record, not a current prohibition. Monthly cadence and post-freeze discipline remain.
title: Backlog: Define ROCKNIX integration and selective backport procedure
